This one password opens everything else, so make it long and memorable: several unrelated words work well. If it’s forgotten, nobody can open the database, not even us.
Creating… This takes a few seconds.
Save it in Google Drive or another storage app to use it on your other devices too, with PocketKeePass or any KeePass app.

PocketKeePass kept a copy of this database from just before its last save here, on %1$s.
A save here was cut short on %1$s. PocketKeePass kept what it was writing, with your latest changes.

This replaces %1$s with the copy from %2$s. Changes made after that, here or on another device, will be lost.\n\nIf the file is still syncing from another device, wait for it to finish first, or choose “Save as new file” instead, which leaves the file alone.
The backup was restored. Unlock it as usual.
PocketKeePass couldn\'t write the backup into the database file. Save it as a new file instead.
PocketKeePass couldn\'t save the backup into that file. Try another location.
Unlocking… This can take a few seconds.
PocketKeePass can\'t open the database file anymore. It may have been moved, renamed, or deleted. Choose it again.
Biometric unlock was turned off because the fingerprints, face, or screen lock on this device changed. Unlock with your master password, then turn it back on in settings.
Biometric unlock was turned off because this database\'s master password or key file changed. Unlock with the new one, then turn it back on in settings.

resources.string: PocketKeePass can\'t open the key file anymore. It may have been moved, renamed, or deleted. Remove it and add it again.
Searches titles, usernames, URLs, notes, and tags. Passwords and other protected fields are never searched.
This entry is in the recycle bin.
“%1$s” goes to the recycle bin. You can move it back out from there.
“%1$s” and everything in it go to the recycle bin. You can move them back out from there.
“%1$s” is deleted for good. This can\'t be undone.
“%1$s” and everything in it are deleted for good. This can\'t be undone.
Everything in the recycle bin is deleted for good. This can\'t be undone. A new recycle bin appears the next time you delete something.

This database uses the older KDBX 3 format, and PocketKeePass only saves KDBX 4. Upgrading keeps everything in it. KeePass 2.35 or later, KeePassXC 2.3 or later, and current KeePass apps open KDBX 4, but apps that only know KDBX 3 won\'t open the file after you save.
Your changes aren\'t saved to the file.
You\'re offline. Your changes are kept on this phone and go into the file once you\'re back online.

Another app or device changed the database file, and PocketKeePass can\'t combine those changes with yours: the file may have a new master password, hold another database, or be damaged. Saving now would replace it with yours.\n\nYour changes stay here until the database locks.

PocketKeePass can\'t write to the database file. It may have been moved or deleted, or the storage app may only allow reading it.\n\nYour changes stay here until the database locks. Save a copy to keep them.
The file didn\'t read back correctly after saving, so the storage app may not have stored it properly. Try again, or save a copy to be safe.\n\nYour changes stay here until the database locks.
%1$s\n\nYour changes stay here until the database locks.
Saved a copy. The database still opens from its old file.
Your changes aren\'t saved to the file yet. Locking discards them.
Can\'t read the file right now. Changes from other devices will come in once it can.
The master password was changed on another device. Lock, then unlock with the new one.
The database\'s security settings were changed on another device. Lock, then unlock it again to take in the changes.
The file now holds a different database. Lock, then unlock it again.
Your last change was saved to the file at %1$s.
Nothing has been changed on this phone since unlocking.
Last checked for changes from other devices %1$s.
Last changes from another device came in at %1$s: %2$s.

Every change you make is saved into the file straight away, and %1$s uploads it from there. PocketKeePass can\'t see when %1$s has finished uploading: if this phone is offline, the change reaches other devices once it\'s back online.\n\nWhile PocketKeePass is open, it checks the file every 30 seconds (or pull down on the list to check now) and takes in changes made on other devices. If two devices changed the database at the same time, both sets of changes are kept. When an entry was changed in both places, the newer version is kept and the other goes into its history.

This file is stored on this phone. If another app (such as Syncthing) shares it with other devices, PocketKeePass checks it every 30 seconds while it\'s open and takes in their changes, keeping both sides\' changes when the database was changed in two places.
PocketKeePass can\'t save new logins yet.
These entries are saved for this app or site. Search to use a different one.
No entry is saved for %1$s. Search for the one to use, and check first that this is the app or site you mean: its username and password will be filled in there.
The entry you pick will be filled in to %1$s.

This app says the page is from %1$s. PocketKeePass can\'t check that, so it only offers entries saved for both this app and that website. Check the address yourself before you search for another entry.
That entry has nothing to fill in here.
Unlock this database with a fingerprint or face
Anyone whose fingerprint or face is set up on this phone can then open it. Adding or removing one turns this off, and your master password is always needed to turn it back on.
Set up a fingerprint (or a face unlock that Android rates as strong) in your phone\'s settings to use this.
Ask for the master password again every:
And after every restart of the phone. Typing it now and then keeps you from forgetting it, and means a lost phone takes more than a fingerprint to open.
Next time, open %1$s with a fingerprint or face instead of typing your master password. You can change this any time in settings.
Fill in usernames and passwords in other apps

Android then offers your entries when you tap a login field, in apps and in browsers. Nothing is filled in until you pick an entry. In Chrome, also turn on Settings › Autofill services › Autofill using another service.

Lock when the screen turns off

PocketKeePass opens and saves KeePass databases (.kdbx). KeePass and its file format were created by Dominik Reichl (keepass.info). PocketKeePass is an independent app. It isn\'t made or endorsed by the KeePass project and uses none of its code.
PocketKeePass is written with Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic.
Free and open-source software, licensed under the GPLv3.
Only symbols that sites commonly accept: %1$s
Every symbol on the keyboard: %1$s. Some sites reject a few of these; switch to Common if one does.
No symbols. Use this only if a site rejects all of them; make the password longer to make up for it.
Every kind you choose appears at least once.
Save the passkey in this KeePass database
Asked by %1$s, in a browser PocketKeePass has verified.
Asked by the app %1$s. PocketKeePass can\'t check whether it belongs to %2$s, so only continue if you trust it. It will be allowed to use this passkey from now on.
Allow an app to use a passkey

%1$s wants to sign in to %2$s with the passkey in “%3$s”.
PocketKeePass can\'t check whether this app belongs to %2$s. Only allow it if you trust it: it will be able to use this passkey from now on.
Passkeys need a screen lock, so PocketKeePass can check it\'s you before each use. Set one in Android\'s settings first.
PocketKeePass was locked before the passkey was saved, so it wasn\'t created. Try again.
Another app or device changed the database file since PocketKeePass opened it. Open PocketKeePass to sort that out, then try again.
That passkey isn\'t in the database anymore.
%1$s isn\'t the app this passkey belongs to: an app with that name is linked to it, but signed by someone else. PocketKeePass won\'t let it sign in.
PocketKeePass couldn\'t tell which app is asking.
The sign-in request couldn\'t be read.
Sign in with passkeys kept in PocketKeePass

Android\'s settings decide which apps provide passkeys. Turn PocketKeePass on under Passwords, passkeys & accounts. Passkeys are kept in the database like KeePassXC and KeePassDX keep them, so they work there too.
Passkeys from other apps need Android 14 or later.
